aabriefcase.text: An agentic knowledge-work benchmark of 91 tasks across four multi-week professional scenarios (data science, product management, banking, corporate strategy), where models produce spreadsheets, decks and memos scored by rubric checks plus pairwise judging of analysis and presentation.

aalcr.text: 100 hard text questions from Artificial Analysis that each require reasoning across a set of real documents totalling roughly 100k tokens, spanning company reports, industry reports, government consultations, academia, legal, marketing and survey documents.

activitynetqa.text: 58,000 human-annotated question-answer pairs over 5,800 complex web videos drawn from ActivityNet, for open-ended video question answering.

advbench.text: An adversarial safety set of 500 harmful strings and 500 harmful behavior instructions spanning profanity, threats, misinformation, discrimination, cybercrime and illegal advice, used to measure attack success rates against aligned models.

aegis.text: A content safety dataset of roughly 26,000 human-LLM interaction instances with human annotations, labelled against a taxonomy of 13 critical and 9 sparse risk categories, used to evaluate guardrail and moderation models.

agentdojo.text: A dynamic environment for evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses on tool-using agents, with 97 realistic tasks such as email and e-banking plus 629 security test cases.

agentharm.text: 110 explicitly malicious agent tasks (440 with augmentations) across 11 harm categories such as fraud, cybercrime and harassment, scoring both whether a model refuses and whether a jailbroken agent can still carry the multi-step task out.

agentslastexam.text: A benchmark of over 1,000 long-horizon, economically valuable tasks built with 250+ industry experts, organized into 55 subfields across 13 industry clusters drawn from the O*NET/SOC 2018 occupational taxonomy, with verifiable outcomes.

agieval.text: A benchmark drawn from human-centric standardized exams in English and Chinese, including college entrance exams, law school admission tests, math competitions and lawyer qualification tests, testing understanding, knowledge, reasoning and calculation.

ai2d.text: A set of 4,903 grade school science diagrams from textbooks, annotated with segmentations of their graphical and text elements, paired with multiple-choice questions that require parsing diagram structure to answer.

aider.text: Aider's code editing benchmark, which asks a model to complete 133 Exercism Python exercises from stub code and then repair its work once after seeing unit test errors; it scores both correctness and whether edits are formatted so Aider can apply them.

aiderpolyglot.text: Aider's code-editing benchmark over 225 of the hardest Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust, run through Aider so the model must produce applicable edits to existing files.

aime.text: The American Invitational Mathematics Examination, a 15-question, three-hour competition run by the Mathematical Association of America in which every answer is an integer from 0 to 999.

aime-2024.text: The 30 problems of the 2024 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME I and II), each with an integer answer from 0 to 999, used to test multi-step competition mathematics by exact match.

aime-2025.text: The 30 problems of the 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME I and II), covering algebra, geometry, number theory and combinatorics, each graded by exact match on an integer answer from 0 to 999.

aime26.text: The 30 problems of the 2026 American Invitational Mathematics Examination (15 from AIME I and 15 from AIME II), each with an integer answer from 0 to 999 so grading is exact match.

aishell1.text: An open-source Mandarin speech recognition corpus of roughly 178 hours from 400 speakers, recorded indoors on three devices, used to measure character error rate on its held-out test set.

aishell2.text: A Mandarin speech recognition corpus of 1,000 hours of clean read speech recorded on iOS devices, with separate development and test sets recorded on Android phones and a microphone for channel robustness.

alignbench.text: 683 real-scenario Chinese queries across eight categories with human-verified references, scored by a rule-calibrated multi-dimensional LLM judge that produces chain-of-thought explanations alongside its ratings.

alignbenchv11.text: Version 1.1 of AlignBench, a Chinese alignment benchmark of 683 real-user queries across eight categories, judged by a model with chain-of-thought and rule-calibrated scoring; v1.1 corrected the reference answers on fact-heavy items and added source evidence.

alpacaeval.text: An automatic instruction-following evaluation over 805 instructions drawn from self-instruct, open-assistant, vicuna, koala and hh-rlhf, where an LLM judge picks between the model's output and a reference model's output to give a win rate.

alpacaeval20.text: The second version of AlpacaEval: 805 instructions answered by the model under test and by a GPT-4 Turbo baseline, with a GPT-4 Turbo annotator producing a continuous preference from logprobs, reported as a win rate against the baseline.

amc10.text: The American Mathematics Competitions 10: a 25-question, 75-minute multiple-choice exam for advanced middle and high school students covering algebra, counting, geometry, number theory and probability, excluding calculus and trigonometry.

amc12.text: The American Mathematics Competition 12, a 25-question, 75-minute multiple-choice examination for high school students covering algebra, counting, geometry, number theory and probability.

amc23.text: The 40 problems from the 2023 AMC 12A and 12B competitions, each rewritten with a short numeric answer so that responses can be checked automatically.

androidcontrol.text: 15,283 human demonstrations of everyday tasks across 833 Android apps, each annotated with both a high-level goal and low-level step instructions, used to train and evaluate UI control agents.

androidworld.text: A live Android environment with 116 programmatic tasks across 20 real apps, each parameterized so instructions vary, with per-task initialization and success checking against device state.

apexagents.text: 240 long-horizon professional services tasks set in 31 simulated workplace environments of files and tools, authored by practicing lawyers, consultants and bankers and graded against expert-written rubrics by a language model judge.

apps.text: 10,000 Python coding problems stated in unrestricted natural language, from introductory exercises to competition-level algorithmic challenges, with test cases and human-written reference solutions.

arc.text: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge: 7,787 natural grade-school science multiple-choice questions, partitioned into an Easy set and a Challenge set that keeps only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval and a word co-occurrence baseline.

arc-agi.text: 800 grid puzzles in which a system infers a transformation from about three input/output example pairs and applies it to a new grid, split into training, public, semi-private and private evaluation sets.

arc-agi-2.text: Grid puzzles in which a system infers a transformation from a handful of input/output examples and applies it to a new grid, rebuilt after ARC-AGI-1 to demand harder generalization and resist brute-force program search, with every task verified solvable by people.

arc-challenge.text: The Challenge partition of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge: 2,590 multiple-choice grade-school science questions that both a retrieval solver and a word co-occurrence baseline answered incorrectly.

arcagi1.text: The 2019 Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus: grid puzzles where a handful of input-output example pairs define a transformation rule the solver must infer and apply to a new grid, split into public training, public evaluation, semi-private and private sets.

arcagi3.text: An interactive reasoning benchmark of novel, fully human-solvable game environments, where an agent must learn the rules from experience, plan over long horizons with sparse feedback, and is scored relative to how efficiently humans complete the same games.

arcc.text: The Challenge split of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge: the natural grade-school science multiple-choice questions that both a retrieval-based solver and a word co-occurrence baseline answered incorrectly.

arce.text: The easier of the two splits of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, a 7,787-question set of multiple-choice grade-school science exam questions; the Easy Set holds the questions that retrieval and word co-occurrence baselines answer correctly.

arceasy.text: The easier partition of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, made up of grade-school science questions in multiple-choice form that a retrieval or word co-occurrence baseline can already answer correctly.

arenahard.text: 500 challenging prompts selected automatically from live Chatbot Arena conversations by the BenchBuilder pipeline, with answers scored by an LLM judge against a baseline model.

arenahardv2.text: A 750-prompt automatic evaluation built from Chatbot Arena traffic: 500 hard real-world queries in areas such as software engineering and math plus 250 creative writing queries, with model answers compared by LLM judges.

arkitscenes.text: An RGB-D dataset of indoor scenes captured with the LiDAR sensor on Apple mobile devices, with laser-scanner depth maps and hand-labelled 3D oriented bounding boxes, used for 3D object detection and depth upsampling.

art.text: The Agent Red Teaming benchmark, built from high-impact attacks collected in a large public red-teaming competition against 22 frontier agents across 44 realistic deployment scenarios, measuring how readily prompt injection drives an agent into policy violations such as unauthorized data access.

audiomultichallenge.text: 452 unscripted multi-turn spoken conversations from 47 speakers with 1,712 instance-specific rubrics, extending MultiChallenge to audio and adding a Voice Editing axis for mid-utterance speech repairs and backtracking.

autologi.text: Automatically generated open-ended logic puzzles with controllable difficulty, where candidate answers are checked by a generated verification program rather than multiple choice.

automationbench.text: A Zapier benchmark of business workflow tasks across simulated SaaS applications, where an agent must discover REST endpoints itself, follow layered business policies and coordinate data across systems; grading is programmatic and end-state only.

babyvision.text: 388 items in 22 subclasses testing foundational visual abilities inspired by infant and early-childhood visual development: fine-grained discrimination, spatial perception, visual pattern recognition and visual tracking.

bbeh.text: BIG-Bench Extra Hard: a reasoning benchmark that replaces every task in BIG-Bench Hard with a new task probing a similar skill at much greater difficulty, aimed at general reasoning beyond math and code.

bbh.text: BIG-Bench Hard: a suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks selected because prior language model evaluations on them did not beat the average human rater, many of which require multi-step reasoning.

bbq.text: A hand-built bias benchmark for question answering: author-written question sets covering attested social biases along nine dimensions, asked once with an under-informative context and once with a disambiguating context.

beavertails.text: A human-annotated question-answering dataset that labels helpfulness and harmlessness separately, with safety meta-labels on 333,963 QA pairs and 361,903 expert comparison pairs.

benchcad.text: 17,900 execution-verified CadQuery programs across 106 industrial part families (bevel gears, compression springs, twist drills and others), posed as visual and code question answering, image-to-code generation and instruction-guided code editing.

bfcl.text: An executable evaluation of function calling that mixes static expert-written cases with live community-contributed ones and single- versus multi-turn calls, scoring output by abstract syntax tree comparison and by actually running the call.

bfclv3.text: The third version of the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard, adding multi-turn and multi-step tool use scored by comparing the resulting backend state against ground truth, with categories for missing parameters, missing functions and long distracting context.

bigbenchaudio.text: 1,000 questions adapted from Big Bench Hard into synthetic spoken audio across four task types (formal fallacies, navigate, object counting, web of lies), testing reasoning when the input arrives as speech.

bigcodebench.text: 1,140 Python tasks that require composing calls to functions from 139 libraries across seven domains, testing diverse function calling and following complex instructions.

biolpbench.text: Seeds real biological laboratory protocols with several harmless errors plus one critical error that would make the experiment fail, and asks the model to identify the critical one, with human experts as the reference point.

biomysterybench.text: A bioinformatics research benchmark from Anthropic in which each problem hands the model anonymized biological data files and asks a question that can only be answered by analysing them, with lookup of the source dataset by accession ID disallowed.

birdsql.text: A text-to-SQL benchmark of 12,751 question and SQL pairs over 95 large databases totalling 33.4 GB across 37 professional domains, emphasizing dirty database values, external knowledge and SQL execution efficiency.

bixbench.text: Over 50 real computational biology analysis scenarios with roughly 300 open-answer questions, where an agent must explore the supplied data, run multi-step analyses and interpret the result.

blink.text: Reformats 14 classic computer vision tasks (relative depth, visual correspondence, forensics detection, multi-view reasoning and others) into 3,807 multiple-choice questions over one or more images with visual prompting.

blueprintbench2.text: An Andon Labs eval where an agent sees about 20 interior photos per apartment across 50 apartments and must output a 2D floor plan. Plans are scored by comparing their room and doorway connectivity graph with ground truth, and the agent keeps a notepad across apartments.

bold.text: 23,679 English text-generation prompts drawn from Wikipedia across profession, gender, race, religion and political ideology, scored with automated measures of toxicity, psycholinguistic norms and gender polarity.

boolq.text: A reading comprehension set of 15,942 naturally occurring yes/no questions from user search queries, each paired with a Wikipedia passage that the model must use to decide the answer.

browsecomp.text: A set of 1,266 questions that require an agent to persistently navigate the web for hard-to-find, entangled information. Predicted answers are short and easily verified against a reference answer.

browsecompzh.text: 289 multi-hop questions about the Chinese web, each reverse-engineered from a short verifiable answer such as a date, number or proper noun, with all queries and evidence chains authored natively in Chinese.

c-eval.text: A Chinese-language multiple-choice evaluation suite covering 52 disciplines at four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college and professional), with a C-Eval Hard subset of reasoning-heavy subjects.

c3.text: A free-form multiple-choice Chinese reading comprehension dataset: 19,577 questions over 13,369 dialogues and mixed-genre texts taken from Chinese-as-a-second-language exams.

charadessta.text: A temporal grounding dataset built on Charades, adding 16,128 sentence queries with start and end timestamps over 9,848 videos of everyday indoor activity, so a model must localize the moment a natural language description refers to.

chartmuseum.text: 1,162 expert-annotated questions over real-world charts curated from 184 sources, built to separate questions answerable from the chart's text from those needing genuine visual reasoning.

chartography.text: 100 chart-reading tasks across 12 professional domains using specialist formats such as Kaplan-Meier curves, candlestick charts, contour maps and Sankey diagrams, with questions written by practitioners, verified by other experts, and answered without tools.

chartqa.text: Question answering over bar, line and pie charts, with 9.6K human-written questions plus 23.1K generated from human-written chart summaries, many requiring arithmetic and reference to visual features.

chartqapro.text: 1,948 questions over 1,341 charts gathered from 157 sources, including infographics and dashboards, with multiple-choice, conversational, hypothetical and deliberately unanswerable question types.

charxiv.text: A chart-understanding benchmark of 2,323 natural charts taken from arXiv papers, with human-curated descriptive questions about basic chart elements and reasoning questions that require synthesizing information across complex visual elements.

charxivreasoning.text: The reasoning split of CharXiv: questions over 2,323 real charts handpicked from arXiv papers that require synthesizing information across several visual elements, rather than reading off a single value.

charxivrq.text: The reasoning-question split of CharXiv, whose 2,323 charts are taken from arXiv papers; these questions require synthesizing information across several complex visual elements rather than reading off a single value.

chatbotarena.text: An open platform where a user sends the same prompt to two anonymous models and votes for the better reply, then combines the crowdsourced pairwise comparisons into a head-to-head view of models by human preference.

chinesesimpleqa.text: A Chinese short-answer factuality benchmark covering six major topics and 99 subtopics, with static reference answers and responses graded by an LLM, following the SimpleQA format.

claweval.text: An agent evaluation harness of 300 human-verified tasks in nine categories, split into general, multimodal and multi-turn work, graded on task completion, safety and consistency across repeated trials.

clawevalpass3.text: The Pass^3 metric of Claw-Eval, an agent suite of 300 human-verified tasks graded from execution traces, audit logs and environment snapshots; Pass^3 credits a task only when the agent succeeds on all three trials.

cloningscenarios.text: The 41 Cloning Scenarios of LAB-Bench: multi-step multiple-choice questions drawn from real molecular cloning workflows involving multiple plasmids, DNA fragments, restriction enzymes and cloning methods.

clothoaqa.text: A crowdsourced audio question answering dataset of 1,991 Clotho audio clips of 15 to 30 seconds, each with six questions (yes/no and single-word answers) annotated by three workers.

cluewsc.text: The Chinese Winograd Schema task from the CLUE benchmark: given a sentence, decide whether a pronoun and a noun phrase corefer, using items hand-selected from contemporary Chinese literary works.

cmath.text: Chinese Elementary School Math Word Problems: about 1,700 annotated math word problems drawn from actual Chinese workbooks and exams, covering all six elementary grades.

cmmlu.text: 11,528 Mandarin Chinese multiple-choice questions across 67 subjects spanning STEM, humanities, social science and other fields, including 16 tasks specific to Chinese culture and law.

coco.text: Microsoft COCO: 328k photos of everyday scenes with 2.5 million labeled object instances across 91 categories, annotated with per-instance segmentations for object recognition, localization and scene understanding.

codearena.text: 397 human-curated coding queries across 40 categories and 44 programming languages, judged by a model on how well the response matches human preference rather than by running test cases.

codeforces.text: Problems from Codeforces programming contests, run under contest conditions with the full test suite and the original time and memory limits, with a model's per-contest rank converted into a rating on the same scale used for human competitors.

codexglue.text: A code intelligence benchmark suite from Microsoft of 14 datasets over 10 tasks, grouped into code-to-code (clone and defect detection, completion, refinement, translation), text-to-code, code-to-text and text-to-text.

collie.text: A grammar-based framework for specifying compositional generation constraints at word, sentence, paragraph and passage level, with a compiled dataset of 2,080 instances spanning 13 constraint structures and automatic constraint checking.

commoneval.text: A VoiceBench subset of 200 open-ended, information-seeking spoken questions drawn from CommonVoice recordings, used to test how a voice assistant handles real speech from diverse speakers.

commonsenseqa.text: 12,247 crowd-authored multiple-choice questions built from ConceptNet relations, where the distractors are concepts related to the same source concept so answering requires commonsense knowledge.

commonvoice15.text: Release 15 of Mozilla's Common Voice, a crowdsourced corpus of read speech in over 100 languages where each clip carries the sentence read plus speaker metadata such as accent, age, gender and locale, and up and down votes from community validation.

complexfuncbench.text: A function-calling benchmark across five real-world API scenarios requiring multi-step and constrained calls, with long parameter filling, parameter value reasoning and 128k context, scored by an automatic framework called ComplexEval.

countbench.text: 540 images curated automatically from LAION-400M and then verified by hand, each showing between two and ten instances of an object, with a caption stating the count.

covost.text: A multilingual speech-to-text translation corpus of crowd-sourced read speech covering 11 languages into English, with over 11,000 speakers and more than 60 accents.

covost2.text: A speech-to-text translation corpus built from Common Voice recordings, covering 21 source languages into English and English into 15 languages, with about 2,900 hours of speech.

creativewritingv3.text: 32 creative writing prompts run three times each, with a judge model scoring the outputs against a nine-point rubric and also comparing them pairwise for an Elo rating.

critpt.text: Research-level physics challenges written by active researchers across condensed matter, quantum, astrophysics, high energy and other subfields, answered in guess-resistant formats such as numeric arrays, symbolic expressions and Python functions.

crosscodeeval.text: Cross-file code completion in Python, Java, TypeScript and C#, built from permissively licensed repositories with static analysis used to keep only examples that genuinely require context from other files.

crowspairs.text: 1,508 sentence pairs covering nine kinds of social bias, each pair differing only in whether it states a stereotype about a historically disadvantaged group, used to check which sentence a language model assigns higher likelihood.

crpe.text: Circular-based Relation Probing Evaluation, a multiple-choice benchmark for object relation comprehension in multimodal models, scored under circular permutation of the answer options.

cruxeval.text: A code reasoning benchmark of 800 short Python functions with paired inputs and outputs, split into an input-prediction task and an output-prediction task that require simulating execution rather than writing code.

cruxevali.text: The input-prediction half of CRUXEval: given a short Python function and its output, the model must produce an input that yields that output, over 800 functions of three to thirteen lines.

cruxevalicot.text: The input prediction half of CRUXEval, run with chain-of-thought prompting: given one of 800 short Python functions and an output, the model must produce an input that yields it.

cruxevalo.text: The output-prediction half of CRUXEval: given one of 800 short Python functions and an input, the model must simulate execution and predict what the function returns.

cruxevalocot.text: The output-prediction half of CRUXEval run with chain-of-thought prompting: given one of 800 short Python functions (3 to 13 lines) and an input, the model must predict what the function returns.

csimpleqa.text: A Chinese short-answer factuality benchmark covering six topics and 99 subtopics, with static reference answers kept brief so grading can be automated by a model judge.

cvbench.text: A vision-centric benchmark of about 2,640 multiple-choice questions repurposed from annotated vision datasets, covering 2D spatial relationships and object counting plus 3D depth order and relative distance.

cvebench.text: A sandbox of real web applications carrying critical-severity CVEs, in which an agent is asked to produce a working exploit and the attack is checked automatically against the running app.

cvtg2k.text: 2,000 prompts for complex visual text generation, varying the position, count, length and attributes of the text that an image generator must render, across diverse real-world scenes.

cybench.text: 40 professional capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions covering cryptography, web security, reverse engineering, forensics and exploitation, run in environments where the agent issues shell commands, with subtasks for finer scoring.

cybergym.text: 1,507 real-world vulnerabilities from 188 open-source projects, where an agent is given a codebase and a text description of a bug and must generate a proof-of-concept input that reproduces it.

cyscenariobench.text: A private scenario-based cyber evaluation that scores a model across full multi-stage attack workflows structured as attack trees, at task, path and campaign level, measuring orchestration, branching decisions, constraint adherence and recovery from inconsistent state.

dailyomni.text: A multiple-choice audio-visual question answering benchmark of 684 real-world videos and 1,197 questions across six task families, built so that answering requires aligning what is heard with what is seen over time.

dalle3eval.text: A 170-prompt text-to-image evaluation set released with the DALL-E 3 paper, used for side-by-side human comparisons of generated images on overall preference, prompt-image alignment and visual appeal.

davis.text: The Densely Annotated Video Segmentation dataset and challenge for video object segmentation, with per-pixel object masks across video sequences and a defined evaluation protocol.

deepsearchqa.text: A 900-prompt benchmark for deep research agents on multi-step information-seeking tasks across 17 fields, where the answer is an exhaustive list that must be collated from many sources and de-duplicated.

deepswe.text: 113 original long-horizon software engineering tasks written for the benchmark rather than mined from merged GitHub fixes, spanning 91 repositories across TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript and Rust.

deepswe11.text: A coding agent benchmark whose tasks are written from scratch against active open-source repositories in five languages and never contributed upstream, each graded by a hand-written verifier that accepts any implementation providing the requested functionality.

deepswev11.text: A revision of Datacurve's DeepSWE keeping the same 113 original long-horizon engineering tasks over open-source repositories, but running the agent on a feature branch and grading its committed patch in a separate isolated container.

design2code.text: 484 manually curated real-world webpages, where a multimodal model is given a screenshot and must generate code that renders back into the reference page, scored by automatic similarity metrics and human evaluation.

docvqa.text: Visual question answering over scanned and born-digital document images: 50,000 natural language questions on 12,767 page images, requiring OCR, layout and text reasoning to answer.

dpgbench.text: 1,000 dense prompts for text-to-image models, each describing several objects with distinct attributes and relationships, used to check how faithfully a generated image follows a long instruction.

drawbench.text: A set of roughly 200 text-to-image prompts in 11 categories, probing colors, counting, spatial relations, rendered text, misspellings and unusual object interactions, judged by human raters for fidelity and image-text alignment.

drop.text: A 96k-question English reading comprehension benchmark whose questions require discrete operations over a paragraph, such as addition, counting, sorting or resolving a reference to several positions in the text.

ds1000.text: A thousand data science coding problems drawn from StackOverflow across seven Python libraries such as NumPy and Pandas, checked with multi-criteria tests and reworded to defend against memorization.

dynamath.text: A visual math benchmark of 501 seed questions written as Python programs that generate many concrete variants with altered numbers, function graphs and other visual or textual details, measuring how robustly a model answers across variants.

eclektic.text: A cross-lingual knowledge transfer benchmark in 12 languages: fact-seeking questions are built from Wikipedia articles that exist in one language but not the others, so answering in another language requires carrying the fact across languages.

egoschema.text: Over 5,000 human-curated multiple-choice questions derived from Ego4D, each asking a model to pick one of five answers about a three-minute egocentric video clip, covering more than 250 hours of footage.

embspatial.text: Multiple-choice questions generated automatically from annotated 3D scenes in MP3D, AI2-THOR and ScanNet, covering six egocentric spatial relations: above, below, left, right, close and far.

eqbench.text: A set of English questions in which a model predicts how intensely characters in a dialogue feel each of several emotions, with the predicted values compared against a reference.

erqa.text: 400 multiple-choice questions interleaving images and text, released by Google DeepMind with Gemini Robotics, covering spatial reasoning and world knowledge in real-world robotics scenarios.

evalplus.text: Rebuilds HumanEval and MBPP with automatically generated extra test inputs (about 80x more tests for HumanEval+ and 35x for MBPP+) so that code passing the original tests but wrong on edge cases is caught.

exploitbench.text: A cybersecurity agent benchmark that breaks exploitation into 16 deterministically graded flags, forming a ladder from reaching vulnerable code and triggering a crash through arbitrary read and write and control-flow hijack up to arbitrary code execution.

exploitgym.text: 898 real-world vulnerabilities across userspace programs, the V8 JavaScript engine and the Linux kernel. Given a vulnerability and a proof-of-concept trigger input, an agent must craft a working exploit achieving unauthorized code execution, with configurable security defenses.

factscore.text: A factual precision metric for long-form generation that splits a generated passage into atomic facts and measures the fraction supported by a reliable knowledge source, with an automated retrieval-plus-model estimator standing in for human annotation.

factsgrounding.text: 1,719 examples pairing a long source document with a user request and an instruction to use only that document, judged in two stages by LLM raters for whether the answer addresses the request and whether every claim is grounded in the document.

figqa.text: A LAB-Bench subtask of multiple-choice questions about figures from biology papers, testing whether a model can read and reason over scientific visualizations.

financeagentv11.text: A benchmark of 537 expert-written questions covering entry-level financial analyst work, from simple retrieval to market research and projections, built with Stanford researchers and industry practitioners.

financeagentv2.text: An expanded rebuild of the Finance Agent benchmark with 927 expert-reviewed questions over public company filings and transcripts, split into public, private validation and held-out test sets.

fleurs.text: An n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 translation benchmark, with roughly 12 hours of supervised speech per language, used for speech recognition, language identification, translation and retrieval.

fleursasr.text: Speech recognition on FLEURS, an n-way parallel spoken dataset in 102 languages built on the FLoRes-101 translation benchmark with roughly 12 hours of supervised speech per language.

fleursen.text: The English portion of FLEURS, a parallel read-speech corpus covering 102 languages with roughly 12 hours of supervision each, built on the FLoRes-101 translation set and used for speech recognition.

flickr30k.text: About 31,000 photographs collected from Flickr, each paired with five human-written English captions, used to evaluate image captioning, visual grounding and cross-modal retrieval.

flores.text: A many-way parallel machine translation evaluation set built from Wikipedia sentences and translated by professional translators into a large set of languages, so any translation direction can be scored on aligned references.

flores200.text: 3,001 sentences drawn from 842 web articles and professionally translated into 200 languages, giving an aligned test set for machine translation in tens of thousands of language directions.

frames.text: 824 multi-hop questions from Google that each require synthesizing two to fifteen Wikipedia articles, testing factuality, retrieval and reasoning together in one end-to-end evaluation of retrieval-augmented systems.

frontierscienceresearch.text: The research track of FrontierScience: open-ended PhD-level sub-tasks of real scientific work in physics, chemistry and biology, written and verified by working scientists and graded against granular rubrics covering the solution process, not just the final answer.

frontierswe.text: Ultra long-horizon coding agent tasks drawn from real technical domains (implementation, performance engineering, scientific computing, visual reasoning and AI research), each given a 20 hour budget and graded on a continuous scale rather than pass or fail.

fullduplexbench.text: A benchmark for full-duplex spoken dialogue models that measures interactive behaviours with automatic metrics: pause handling, backchanneling, turn-taking and interruption management.

gaokaobench.text: A Chinese evaluation built from questions in the GAOKAO college entrance examination, mixing objective and subjective questions, run zero-shot with human scoring used for the subjective parts.

gaokaomathcloze.text: The Gaokao-Math-Cloze task from AGIEval: fill-in-the-blank mathematics questions taken from the Chinese national college entrance exam, where the model writes the answer rather than choosing from options.

gaokaomathqa.text: The Gaokao-MathQA subtask of AGIEval: 351 Chinese high school mathematics multiple-choice questions taken from the Gaokao college entrance exam, covering sets, complex numbers, vectors, sequences, geometry and probability.

gdppdf.text: 100 prompts paired with real professional PDFs from ten occupational areas such as finance, healthcare, legal and construction, asking a model to parse and synthesize long documents; outputs are graded against per-task rubrics.

gdpval.text: Real work tasks from 44 occupations in the industries contributing most to GDP, written by professionals averaging 14 years of experience, with model deliverables blind-compared against the human ones by expert graders.

gdpvalaa.text: Artificial Analysis's agentic run of OpenAI's GDPval tasks: models get shell access and web browsing to produce real work deliverables (documents, spreadsheets, slides, diagrams) for occupations across nine industries, graded by blind pairwise LLM judging.

gdpvalaaelo.text: Artificial Analysis's agentic run of OpenAI's GDPval tasks across 44 occupations and nine industries, where models use a shell and web browsing to produce real deliverables that an LLM judge compares blind in pairs, aggregated into an Elo rating.

gdpvalaav2.text: Artificial Analysis's agentic harness over OpenAI's GDPval task set: models get shell access and web browsing to produce finished documents, slides, spreadsheets and diagrams for 220 professional tasks, graded by blind pairwise LLM judging.

geneval.text: An object-focused framework for text-to-image evaluation that runs an object detector over generated images to check compositional properties named in the prompt: object co-occurrence, position, count and color.

gigaspeech.text: A multi-domain English speech recognition corpus of about 10,000 hours of transcribed audio for supervised training, drawn from audiobooks, podcasts and YouTube, with professionally transcribed development and test sets.

globalmmlu.text: A 42-language version of MMLU with translations checked by professional and community annotators, split into culturally sensitive and culturally agnostic question subsets.

globalpiqa.text: A hand-built commonsense reasoning benchmark covering 141 language varieties across 19 language families and 24 writing systems, with a culturally specific non-parallel split and a parallel split translated into 131 varieties, validated by native speakers.

gpqa.text: 448 multiple-choice questions written by domain experts in biology, physics and chemistry, validated so that skilled non-experts cannot answer them even with unrestricted web access.

gpqa-diamond.text: The hardest curated subset of GPQA: 198 multiple-choice biology, chemistry and physics questions written by domain experts, kept only when both expert annotators answered correctly and most non-expert validators did not.

gqa.text: A compositional visual question answering dataset of 22 million questions over 113,000 real-world images, generated from dense scene graphs so each question has a logical program and controlled answer distribution.

graphwalks.text: Fills the context window with a directed graph of hexadecimal hashes and asks the model to run a breadth-first search from a random node and return every node at a given depth, forcing reasoning across many positions at once.

graphwalksbfs.text: A long-context reasoning task that fills the context window with a directed graph of hexadecimal hashes and asks the model to run a breadth-first search from a random node and return every node at a given depth.

graphwalksparents.text: The parents task of Graphwalks, a long-context evaluation where the model reads a directed graph given as an edge list and must return every node with an edge leading into a named node, scored by F1 against the true node set.

gsm8k.text: 8,500 grade school math word problems written by human authors, split 7.5K train and 1K test, each taking two to eight steps of elementary arithmetic and paired with a written solution.

hallusionbench.text: 346 images paired with 1,129 expert-written questions arranged into control groups, designed to separate language hallucination (relying on parametric priors) from visual illusion (misreading the image) in vision-language models.

harveylabaa.text: 120 private legal tasks across 24 practice areas in which an agent is given case documents and must produce a deliverable such as a memo, disclosure schedule or deposition summary, graded criterion by criterion against a task rubric.

healthbench.text: 5,000 realistic multi-turn health conversations written with 262 physicians, where each response is graded by a model against conversation-specific, physician-written rubric criteria.

healthbenchprofessional.text: An OpenAI HealthBench variant of 525 clinical conversations written for clinician users, spanning consultation, writing and research use cases across 28 specialties, with physician-written reference responses and per-conversation rubric criteria.

hellaswag.text: A commonsense sentence-completion test: given a short context, the model picks the true continuation from four endings, where the wrong endings are machine-generated and selected by adversarial filtering.

hle.text: A benchmark of 2,500 closed-ended questions across dozens of academic subjects, written by subject-matter experts as multiple-choice and short-answer items with unambiguous, automatically gradable solutions that cannot be found by quick internet retrieval.

hmmt.text: The Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, a large US high school math competition; its February contests are used as 30-problem final-answer math evaluations on MathArena.

hmmt2025feb.text: The problem set from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, a high school mathematics competition run in Team, Algebra and Number Theory, Combinatorics, Geometry and Guts rounds.

hmmt2026feb.text: The 33 problems from the February 2026 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, a large US high school mathematics competition, run as a math benchmark on MathArena.

hmmt25.text: The 30 answer-based problems from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, spanning algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, with final answers parsed automatically and checked for symbolic equivalence.

hmmtfeb25.text: The 30 problems of the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, extracted and transcribed to LaTeX by MathArena, covering algebra, geometry, combinatorics and number theory.

hmmtfeb26.text: The 33 short-answer problems from the February 2026 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, spanning algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, transcribed to LaTeX and graded by comparing the model's boxed final answer to the official one.

hmmtnov25.text: The 30 problems of the November 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament, extracted and converted to LaTeX by MathArena and used as a math evaluation with short verifiable answers.

hrbench4k.text: The 4K half of HR-Bench, a benchmark of true high-resolution images built to test whether a multimodal model can perceive fine detail without the information loss caused by downsampling.

huggingfaceopenllmleaderboard.text: A Hugging Face leaderboard that runs a fixed suite of public benchmarks on submitted open models through the EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness, so every submission is evaluated under the same prompts and settings.

humaneval.text: A set of 164 hand-written Python programming problems, each with a function signature, docstring and unit tests, scored by executing the generated code against those tests rather than by text matching.

humanevalfim.text: A fill-in-the-middle variant of HumanEval that masks spans from the canonical solutions and asks the model to reconstruct the missing code from the surrounding prefix and suffix, scored by the original unit tests.

humanevalmul.text: The HumanEval Python problems translated into seven further languages, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript, C#, Bash and JavaScript, and run against each language's test cases.

humanevalpython.text: The Python original of HumanEval: hand-written programming problems in which the model synthesizes a function body from its signature and docstring, judged by running unit tests for functional correctness.

hypersim.text: A photorealistic synthetic dataset of 77,400 images across 461 indoor scenes with per-pixel ground truth for semantic instance segmentation, scene geometry, materials, lighting and camera pose.

ifbench.text: An instruction-following benchmark built on 58 new verifiable output constraints (format, length, keyword and structural requirements) that were held out of training, testing whether models generalize to unseen constraints.

ifeval.text: About 500 prompts built from 25 types of verifiable instructions (for example "write more than 400 words" or "mention a keyword at least 3 times"), checked by deterministic programs instead of human or model judges.

imagenet.text: The object recognition benchmark behind the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge, covering image classification and object detection over hundreds of object categories and millions of labelled photographs.

imagenet1k.text: The 1,000-class ImageNet subset used in the ILSVRC image classification task, with 1,281,167 training, 50,000 validation and 100,000 test photographs labelled by WordNet synset.

imageneta.text: A set of natural, unmodified photographs from ImageNet classes selected by adversarial filtration because classifiers misclassify them, used to test image recognition robustness.

imagenetr.text: 30,000 artistic and stylized renditions (art, cartoons, graffiti, origami, sculptures, tattoos, toys and more) of 200 ImageNet classes, used to test classification robustness to distribution shift.

imagenetv2.text: Three replacement ImageNet test sets of 10,000 images each, newly collected from Flickr and filtered by crowd workers following the original ImageNet protocol, to test generalization beyond the reused validation set.

imo25.text: The six problems of the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad, where a model must write a full proof for each and experienced human judges grade the write-up on the official scale.

imoanswerbench.text: 400 past olympiad problems with short verifiable answers, 100 each in algebra, combinatorics, geometry and number theory, altered by experts so they cannot be answered from memory.

include.text: 197,243 multiple-choice questions drawn from local academic, professional and licensing exams in 44 languages and 15 scripts, testing regional and cultural knowledge rather than translated English material.

infographicvqa.text: Question answering over infographic images, requiring joint reasoning over document layout, text, graphical elements and embedded data visualizations, with many questions needing basic arithmetic.

infovqa.text: InfographicVQA: visual question answering over infographic images, where questions require jointly reasoning across document layout, textual content, graphical elements and data visualizations, plus elementary arithmetic.

instructttsevalen.text: The English split of InstructTTSEval, which tests natural-language style control in text-to-speech across three levels (acoustic parameter specification, descriptive style directive and role play), with generated speech judged automatically by Gemini.

instructttsevalzh.text: The Chinese half of InstructTTSEval, 3,000 instruction-following text-to-speech test cases split across acoustic parameter specification, descriptive style directives and role-play, each with reference audio and judged automatically by Gemini.

jobbench.text: 130 agentic tasks across 35 occupations, chosen as workflows experts want delegated. Each task is packaged as a workspace of heterogeneous reference files, and outputs are graded by a chain of fact-anchored rubrics averaging about 36 binary criteria.

kitti.text: A benchmark suite recorded from an instrumented car driving through Karlsruhe, rural roads and highways with stereo cameras, a Velodyne laser scanner and GPS, covering stereo, optical flow, visual odometry, 3D object detection, tracking, depth estimation and segmentation.

kmmlu.text: A Korean knowledge benchmark of 35,030 expert-level multiple-choice questions across 45 subjects, collected from original Korean exams rather than translated from English.

labbench.text: Over 2,400 multiple-choice questions on practical biology research tasks, grouped into subsets for literature extraction, database and supplementary-information lookup, DNA sequence manipulation, figure and table reasoning, and protocol design.

lambada.text: Narrative passages from novels where the final word is predictable to a human who reads the whole passage but not to one who sees only the last sentence, so the model must track the broader discourse.

lcbv6.text: Release v6 of LiveCodeBench, 1,055 competitive programming problems scraped from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces contests held between May 2023 and April 2025 and checked against hidden tests.

librispeech.text: A corpus of roughly 1,000 hours of read English speech at 16 kHz, segmented and aligned from LibriVox public domain audiobooks, used for training and evaluating speech recognition systems.

librispeechclean.text: The clean split of LibriSpeech, read English speech from public domain audiobooks, holding the recordings with clearer acoustics as opposed to the harder 'other' split.

librispeechother.text: The harder half of the LibriSpeech read-audiobook speech recognition corpus: speakers were ranked by the word error rate of a WSJ acoustic model and split in the middle, with the higher-error speakers placed in the "other" sets.

librispeechtestclean.text: The clean test split of LibriSpeech, 2,620 read-speech utterances from LibriVox audiobooks by speakers whose word error rate under a reference model placed them in the easier half of the corpus.

librispeechtestother.text: The harder test split of LibriSpeech, read English speech from LibriVox audiobooks. Speakers were ranked by the word error rate of a baseline recognizer and the higher-error half was assigned to the 'other' subsets.

lingoqa.text: A visual question answering benchmark for autonomous driving built from 28K short video scenarios and 419K annotations, scored with a trained truthfulness classifier called Lingo-Judge.

livebench.text: A contamination-limited benchmark whose questions are refreshed from recent math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles and datasets, spanning math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following and data analysis, and scored against objective ground truth rather than an LLM judge.

livecodebench.text: A continuously updated coding benchmark that collects new problems from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces over time, so models can be scored on time-windowed slices to limit contamination, and covers self-repair, code execution and test output prediction alongside generation.

livecodebenchv5.text: The v5 release of LiveCodeBench: 880 competitive programming problems collected from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces between May 2023 and January 2025, each tagged with a release date so models can be scored only on problems published after their training cutoff.

livecodebenchv6.text: The sixth release window of LiveCodeBench: 1,055 competitive programming problems published between May 2023 and April 2025 on LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces, dated so contaminated problems can be filtered out.

llamaquestions.text: A spoken question answering set of 300 open-domain world knowledge questions generated by prompting LLaMA-7B and rendered to audio with text-to-speech, so a model must answer from the recording.

lmarena.text: A crowdsourced evaluation platform where users submit a prompt, see responses from two anonymous models side by side, and vote for the better one; the votes are aggregated into public leaderboards per category.

loft.text: Long-context tasks scaling to millions of tokens that recast retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation and SQL-style compositional reasoning as problems solved entirely inside the model's context window.

logicvista.text: 448 multiple-choice questions that test five kinds of logical reasoning (deductive, inductive, numerical, spatial and mechanical) over visual inputs such as diagrams, patterns, graphs, tables, 3D shapes and puzzles, each annotated with a human-written rationale.

longbench.text: 21 bilingual English and Chinese datasets in six categories (single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks and code completion), averaging about 6,711 English words per input.

longbenchchat.text: A long context alignment benchmark made of real user queries whose inputs run from 10k to 100k tokens, with model responses scored by GPT-4 rather than by string matching.

longbenchv2.text: 503 multiple-choice questions over contexts of 8k to 2M words, covering single- and multi-document QA, long in-context learning, long dialogue history, code repositories and long structured data.

longtextbench.text: A benchmark introduced with X-Omni for measuring how accurately an image generation model renders long passages of text inside the images it produces, with separate English and Chinese prompt sets.

longvideobench.text: 6,678 human-annotated multiple-choice questions over 3,763 web videos up to an hour long with interleaved subtitles, posed as referring reasoning: each question names a referred context the model must locate and reason over.

lsat.text: The Law School Admission Test, whose scored multiple-choice sections cover Reading Comprehension of long complex passages and Logical Reasoning, plus a separately administered unscored argumentative writing task.

lvbench.text: A long video understanding benchmark built from publicly sourced videos up to two hours long, including TV series, sports broadcasts and surveillance footage, with tasks requiring retrieval and reasoning across the whole recording.

m3exams.text: 12,317 questions taken from real official human exams in nine languages at three educational levels, about 23 percent of which include images that must be read to answer.

makemesay.text: An OpenAI manipulation eval framed as a game: the tested model must get a second model, simulating a human, to say a secret codeword within 30 turns without that model working out the word or hearing the model say it first.

mask.text: A human-collected benchmark that separates honesty from accuracy by first eliciting a model's belief on a proposition and then pressuring it to contradict that belief, measuring whether the model lies.

math.text: 12,500 competition mathematics problems drawn from high school contests such as AMC 10, AMC 12 and AIME, each with a full LaTeX statement, a step-by-step solution and a standardized final answer for automatic checking.

math-500.text: A 500-problem subset of the MATH competition-mathematics dataset, selected by OpenAI for the Let's Verify Step by Step paper, spanning seven subjects and five difficulty levels with reference step-by-step solutions.

math23k.text: 23,161 Chinese math word problems crawled from online education sites for elementary school pupils, each a one-unknown linear problem labelled with an equation template and an answer.

matharenaapex.text: Twelve very hard final-answer math problems drawn from 2025 competitions, half from final-answer contests and half converted from proof-based ones, filtered by testing candidates against frontier models and keeping only those that survived.

mathodyssey.text: A mathematics benchmark of problems written by experts at high school, university and olympiad level, built to cover a wider range of subject areas than earlier math evaluation sets.

mathverse.text: 2,612 diagram-based math problems in plane geometry, solid geometry and functions, each rewritten into six versions that shift information between the text and the diagram to test whether a model actually reads the figure.

mathvision.text: 3,040 mathematics problems with visual context taken from real math competitions, spanning 16 disciplines and five difficulty levels, testing multimodal mathematical reasoning.

mathvisionfull.text: The complete MATH-Vision set of 3,040 visual mathematics problems taken from real competitions, spanning 16 mathematical subjects and five difficulty levels, where the diagram is needed to solve the problem.

mathvista.text: A benchmark of 6,141 examples testing mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, drawn from 28 existing multimodal datasets plus three new ones, spanning tasks such as geometry problems, algebraic reasoning and scientific chart understanding.

mathvistamini.text: The 1,000-example testmini split of MathVista, a visual mathematical reasoning benchmark assembled from 28 existing multimodal datasets plus three new ones, covering geometry diagrams, function plots, charts, tables, scientific figures and natural images.

mbpp.text: 974 short Python programming tasks designed to be solvable by entry-level programmers, where the model must synthesize a program from a natural language description.

mbppplus.text: The MBPP Python programming problems re-tested by EvalPlus, which adds roughly 35 times more automatically generated test cases and prunes broken tasks to catch plausible but incorrect solutions.

mcpatlas.text: A benchmark of 1,000 human-written natural language tasks run against 36 production MCP servers exposing 220 tools. Prompts name no server or tool, and answers are graded against atomic factual claims grounded in tool output.

mcpmark.text: 127 expert-written tasks that exercise Model Context Protocol servers such as Notion, GitHub and the filesystem in isolated containers, testing tool selection and multi-step dependency chains with programmatic verification.

medmcqa.text: Over 194,000 multiple-choice questions from the Indian AIIMS and NEET PG medical entrance exams, spanning 21 medical subjects and about 2,400 topics, each with options and a written explanation.

medxpertqamm.text: The multimodal subset of MedXpertQA: expert-level medical exam questions that pair diverse images with rich clinical context such as patient records and examination results, rather than caption-derived question and answer pairs.

meld.text: About 13,000 utterances from 1,433 multi-party dialogues in the TV series Friends, each labelled with an emotion and a sentiment, with aligned audio, video and text.

mgsm.text: 250 grade school math word problems drawn from GSM8K and hand-translated into ten typologically diverse languages, used to test chain-of-thought reasoning outside English.

mind2web.text: A web agent dataset of over 2,000 open-ended tasks collected from 137 real websites across 31 domains, where an agent must follow a language instruction through a sequence of actions on the page.

minif2f.text: 488 formal statements of Olympiad-level mathematics problems from AIME, AMC and the IMO plus high school and undergraduate material, written for several proof assistants (Metamath and Lean, with partial Isabelle and HOL Light support) so theorem provers can be compared across systems.

miniwob.text: Over 100 simulated web interaction environments exposed through the Gymnasium API, in which an agent drives a browser to complete small tasks such as clicking controls, filling forms and working through an email inbox.

miracl.text: A multilingual ad hoc retrieval dataset covering 18 languages, with over 700k relevance judgments by native speakers for about 77k queries over Wikipedia, where query and corpus share a language.

mlebench.text: 75 Kaggle machine learning engineering competitions packaged as agent tasks, covering dataset preparation, model training and experiment running, scored against the original competition leaderboards.

mls.text: Multilingual LibriSpeech, a read-audiobook corpus in eight languages derived from LibriVox, with about 44,500 hours of English and roughly 6,000 hours across the other languages, used for speech recognition evaluation.

mlsbenchlite.text: The 30-task subset of MLS-Bench, in which an agent must propose a targeted improvement to one component of a machine learning system, such as a loss function, and show that it transfers across models, datasets and scales.

mmar.text: 1,000 audio-question-answer triplets from real internet videos mixing sound, music and speech, organized into four reasoning layers (signal, perception, semantic and cultural) and paired with chain-of-thought rationales.

mmau.text: 10,000 audio clips with multiple-choice questions over speech, environmental sounds and music, covering 27 tasks that mix information extraction with reasoning that needs domain knowledge.

mmbench.text: A vision-language benchmark of about 3,000 single-answer multiple-choice questions across 20 ability dimensions, scored with CircularEval, which re-asks each question with the choices circularly shifted and counts it correct only if every pass is right.

mmbenchcn.text: The Chinese half of MMBench, a multiple-choice vision-language benchmark whose questions are translated in parallel with the English set, scored with the CircularEval protocol that rotates answer options across repeated passes.

mmbenchen.text: The English half of MMBench, a bilingual multiple-choice vision-language benchmark spanning many ability dimensions and scored with CircularEval, which re-asks each question with the options rotated.

mmbenchenv11.text: The English split of MMBench v1.1, a data-quality revision of MMBench: multiple-choice vision-language questions organized around 20 ability dimensions and scored with CircularEval, which re-asks each question with the options rotated.

mme.text: A multimodal evaluation of 14 subtasks split into perception and cognition abilities, with every instruction-answer pair written by hand so that no public dataset annotations leak into the questions.

mmerealworld.text: 29,429 human-annotated question-answer pairs over 13,366 high-resolution images, covering 43 subtasks across five real-world scenarios, annotated by professional annotators rather than by models.

mmlongbenchdoc.text: 1,062 expert-written questions over 130 long PDFs averaging 49 pages, where the evidence may be text, an image, a chart, a table or layout structure, and about a third of the questions need evidence from more than one page.

mmlu.text: A multiple-choice test of knowledge and problem solving across 57 subjects, including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science and law, ranging from elementary to advanced professional difficulty.

mmlu-pro.text: A harder rebuild of MMLU with over 12,000 questions across 14 domains, expanding each question from four answer options to ten and removing trivial or noisy items so that reasoning rather than recall is required.

mmlu-redux.text: A manually re-annotated subset of MMLU covering all 57 subjects, in which each question was rechecked against its original source and labelled with an error type so that ground-truth mistakes can be excluded.

mmluanatomy.text: The anatomy subject of MMLU: four-option multiple-choice questions on human anatomy, one of the 57 subject splits in the Massive Multitask Language Understanding benchmark.

mmluclinicalknowledge.text: The clinical knowledge subject of MMLU: four-option multiple-choice questions on clinical medicine and nursing practice, covering procedures, anatomy, pharmacology and diagnosis.

mmlucollegebiology.text: The college biology subject of MMLU, one of its 57 knowledge tasks, consisting of four-option multiple-choice exam questions (165 in the test split).

mmlucollegemedicine.text: The college medicine subject of MMLU, one of its 57 subject configurations, consisting of four-option multiple-choice questions at undergraduate level answered from the question alone with no supplied passage.

mmlumedicalgenetics.text: The medical genetics subject of MMLU: four-option multiple-choice questions on inheritance patterns, chromosomal abnormalities, enzyme deficiencies, genetic disorders and molecular diagnostic techniques, with 116 test items.

mmluprofessionalmedicine.text: The Professional Medicine subject of MMLU, made up of US Medical Licensing Examination style multiple-choice questions on diagnosis, pharmacotherapy and disease prevention.

mmluprox.text: A multilingual extension of MMLU-Pro with 11,829 parallel questions rendered in 29 languages, machine translated and then reviewed by experts for terminology and cultural fit.

mmlustem.text: The science, technology, engineering and mathematics slice of MMLU, covering 18 of its 57 multiple-choice subject tests.

mmmlu.text: The MMLU test set rendered into 14 languages by professional human translators, giving 14,042 parallel multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects in each language.

mmmtbench.text: 92 multi-turn conversations over charts, tables, PDF pages, diagrams and other images, with each turn rated one to ten by a judge model for correctness and completeness against a reference answer.

mmmu.text: About 11.5K college-level multimodal questions drawn from exams, quizzes and textbooks across six disciplines, pairing images such as charts, diagrams, maps and chemical structures with questions that need domain knowledge and reasoning.

mmmupro.text: A harder rebuild of MMMU that removes questions a text-only model can answer, expands the answer options, and adds a vision-only setting where the question itself is embedded in the image.

mmmuprostandard.text: The standard setting of MMMU-Pro, built from MMMU by discarding questions that text-only models can answer and enlarging the list of candidate options, with image and question supplied separately rather than rendered into one screenshot.

mmmuprovision.text: The vision-only setting of MMMU-Pro, in which each multi-discipline exam question is embedded as text inside a screenshot image so the model must read and reason from the image alone.

mmmuval.text: The 900-question validation split of MMMU, college-level multimodal exam questions across six disciplines and 30 subjects, with figures such as charts, diagrams, maps, music sheets and chemical structures.

mmsearchplus.text: 311 browsing tasks that cannot be solved from text alone: an agent must pull fine-grained spatial and temporal cues out of an image and carry them through rounds of search to recover facts such as the event, date or venue.

mmstar.text: 1,500 human-vetted multimodal questions selected so that each genuinely requires the image and shows little training-data leakage, covering six core vision-language capabilities and 18 finer axes.

mmsu.text: 5,000 audio-question-answer triplets across 47 spoken language tasks, covering phonetics, prosody, rhetoric, syntax, semantics and paralinguistics, each posed as a four-option multiple-choice question over an audio clip.

mmtbench.text: 31,325 multiple-choice visual questions spanning 32 meta-tasks and 162 subtasks, covering visual recognition, localization, reasoning and planning across many multimodal scenarios.

mmteb.text: A community-built expansion of MTEB for text embedding models, covering over 500 quality-controlled evaluation tasks in more than 250 languages, including instruction following, long-document retrieval and code retrieval.

mmvet.text: An open-ended multimodal benchmark built around six core vision-language skills (recognition, knowledge, spatial awareness, language generation, OCR and math) and 16 combinations of them, with free-form answers graded by an LLM judge.

mmvp.text: A visual benchmark built from CLIP-blind image pairs that look similar to CLIP but differ clearly to people, posing simple questions across nine basic visual patterns to expose perception failures in multimodal models.

mmvu.text: A video understanding benchmark of 3,000 expert-annotated questions over specialized-domain videos spanning 27 subjects in science, healthcare, humanities and social sciences, and engineering.

motionbench.text: A video benchmark focused on fine-grained motion perception, with six categories of motion-oriented questions over web, movie, synthetic and other video sources.

mrcr.text: A long-context test in which a model reads a synthetic multi-turn conversation containing 2, 4 or 8 identical requests and must reproduce the i-th response to that request, distinguishing between near-identical distractors.

mscoco.text: The Microsoft COCO dataset of about 328,000 everyday scene images with 2.5 million labeled instances across 91 object categories, annotated with per-instance segmentation masks for object recognition in context.

mt-bench.text: 80 multi-turn questions across common use cases, used to test instruction following and conversation over two turns, with responses graded by a strong language model acting as judge.

mteb.text: A text embedding benchmark spanning eight task types (classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity, summarization and bitext mining) over 58 datasets and 112 languages.

mtebcode.text: The code slice of MTEB: 12 retrieval tasks spanning popular programming languages, covering code search, text-to-SQL and code feedback, used to score text embedding models.

mtebengv2.text: A 41-task English text embedding benchmark covering retrieval, classification, semantic similarity, clustering and reranking, cut down from MTEB v1 and made zero-shot by excluding training-common sets such as MS MARCO and Natural Questions.

mtebmultilingual.text: The highly multilingual benchmark defined in MMTEB: 132 text embedding tasks covering more than 250 languages, selected from over 500 candidates by dropping machine-translated, unlicensed and highly predictable datasets.

muirbench.text: 2,600 multiple-choice questions over 11,264 images covering 12 multi-image tasks and 10 kinds of relation between images, with each question paired to an unanswerable variant that differs only slightly, to test robustness.

multichallenge.text: A multi-turn conversation benchmark from Scale AI covering four challenges: instruction retention, inference memory of user information, reliable versioned editing, and self-coherence. Final responses are graded by an LLM judge against instance-level rubrics.

multiif.text: An instruction-following benchmark that extends IFEval to 4,501 three-turn conversations translated into eight languages, testing whether constraints are still obeyed as turns accumulate.

multilinguallibrispeech.text: A speech corpus derived from LibriVox audiobooks in eight languages, with about 44,500 hours of English and roughly 6,000 hours across the others, used for automatic speech recognition evaluation.

multilingualmmlu.text: MMLU's 57-subject multiple-choice test set translated out of English so the same questions can be scored in other languages. OpenAI's MMMLU release covers 14 languages using professional human translators.

multipl-e.text: A system that translates the HumanEval and MBPP Python code generation benchmarks, including their unit tests, into 18 other programming languages.

multiplehumaneval.text: The HumanEval problems translated by MultiPL-E into 18 further programming languages, so the same unit-test-driven code generation tasks can be scored outside Python.

multiplembpp.text: The MBPP Python programming problems translated by MultiPL-E, along with their unit tests, into 18 additional programming languages so the same tasks can be scored language by language.

musiccaps.text: 5,500 music clips paired with rich free-text descriptions written by human experts, released with MusicLM and used to evaluate text-to-music generation and music captioning.

mvbench.text: 20 video understanding tasks built by converting image tasks into temporal ones, posed as multiple-choice questions that cannot be answered from a single frame.

mvp.text: About 55,000 multiple-choice video questions on physical world understanding, each paired with a visually similar video carrying the same question but the opposite answer, so a model scores only by getting both members of the pair right.

naturalquestions.text: Open-domain question answering on real anonymized queries issued to Google search, where annotators marked a long answer (a paragraph) and a short answer on a Wikipedia page, or null when the page has neither.

needleinahaystack.text: A long context retrieval probe that hides a fact in a large document and sweeps context length against the depth at which the fact is buried, scoring whether the model can recover it at each combination.

nextqa.text: Video question answering aimed at causal and temporal action reasoning rather than scene description, posed in both multiple-choice and open-ended form.

nl2repo.text: Repository-level generation from scratch: given only a natural language requirements document and an empty workspace, the agent must design the architecture, manage dependencies and produce an installable Python library, scored by test pass rate.

nl2repobench.text: A long-horizon coding benchmark that hands an agent a single natural language requirements document and an empty workspace and asks for a fully installable Python library, scoring the result by how many of the reference tests pass.

nocaps.text: A novel object captioning benchmark of 166,100 human-written captions for 15,100 Open Images photos, many containing object classes with no captioned training examples in COCO.

nq.text: Natural Questions: real anonymized Google search queries paired with a Wikipedia page, where annotators marked a long answer (usually a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities), or null if the page contains neither.

nyuv2.text: An indoor scene dataset recorded with a Microsoft Kinect, providing 1,449 densely labelled aligned RGB and depth image pairs from 464 scenes plus over 400,000 raw unlabelled frames.

objectnet.text: A test-only object recognition set of 50,000 images across 313 classes, photographed with explicit controls on object rotation, background and viewpoint so that familiar objects appear in unfamiliar poses and settings.

obqa.text: OpenBookQA: about 6,000 multiple-choice questions modelled on open book exams, each solvable by combining one of 1,329 elementary science facts with broader common knowledge.

ocrbench.text: An OCR evaluation suite for multimodal models assembled from 29 datasets, covering text recognition, scene-text and document visual question answering, key information extraction and handwritten mathematical expression recognition.

ocrbenchv2.text: A text-centric multimodal benchmark of 10,000 human-verified question and answer pairs across 31 scenarios, plus a private 1,500-image test set, covering text recognition and localization, handwriting extraction, layout parsing and reasoning over text in images.

ocrvqa.text: Around 207,000 book cover images with over a million question-answer pairs about the title, author, genre and publisher, so answering requires reading the text rendered in the image.

odinw13.text: The 13-dataset subset of Object Detection in the Wild used by GLIP, a set of real-world object detection datasets used to measure zero-shot, few-shot and full-shot transfer of pretrained vision models.

officeqa.text: A Databricks benchmark suite for grounded reasoning over dense financial documents, requiring an agent to find and combine figures across U.S. Treasury Bulletins and federal receipts and expenditures records, graded by fuzzy numeric matching.

officeqapro.text: 133 questions over a corpus of U.S. Treasury Bulletins spanning nearly a century, about 89,000 pages and 26 million numerical values, requiring an agent to parse documents, retrieve the right passages and reason across unstructured text and tables.

ojbench.text: 232 competitive programming problems taken from NOI and ICPC contests, submitted to an online judge so solutions are graded on contest test cases rather than by string matching.

okvqa.text: Over 14,000 visual questions whose answers cannot be read off the image, so a model must draw on external world knowledge in addition to what it sees.

olympiadbench.text: 8,476 bilingual olympiad-level mathematics and physics problems, drawn from competitions and the Chinese college entrance exam, many with diagrams, and annotated by experts with step-by-step reasoning.

omnidocbench.text: A PDF document parsing benchmark covering nine document sources including academic papers, textbooks, handwritten notes and newspapers, with layout and recognition annotations supporting end-to-end, task-specific and attribute-based evaluation.

omnidocbench15.text: Version 1.5 of OmniDocBench, a document parsing benchmark of 1,355 PDF pages across nine document types in English, Chinese and mixed text, with block and span level annotations for layout, tables, formulas and OCR.

omnidocbenchv15.text: Version 1.5 of the OmniDocBench document parsing benchmark: 1,651 PDF pages over 10 document types with 28 block-level and 4 span-level annotation elements, rescanned newspaper and note pages, rebalanced Chinese and English pages, and a hybrid text-formula matching algorithm.

omnigaia.text: A benchmark for omni-modal agents built from an event-graph construction over real data, posing multi-hop queries that require reasoning across video, audio and image inputs together with multi-turn tool use.

oneigbenchen.text: The English prompt set of OneIG-Bench, a text-to-image benchmark scoring generations along separate dimensions: prompt-image alignment, text rendering precision, reasoning-generated content, stylization and diversity.

oneigbenchzh.text: The Chinese prompt set of OneIG-Bench, a text-to-image benchmark whose prompts are scored separately for subject alignment, text rendering, knowledge and reasoning, stylization and diversity.

onlinemind2web.text: A web agent benchmark of 300 diverse, realistic tasks spanning 136 websites, built to evaluate agents in a setting that approximates how real users actually use them.

openai-moderation.text: OpenAI's content moderation evaluation set, built with a taxonomy of undesired content categories such as sexual content, hate, violence, self-harm and harassment, used to test text classifiers.

openbookqa.text: A multiple-choice QA set of about 6,000 questions paired with a small book of 1,329 elementary science facts, where answering requires combining a book fact with broader common knowledge.

openeqa.text: Embodied question answering over more than 1,600 human-written questions about 180-plus real environments, in an episodic memory setting and an active exploration setting, with open-vocabulary answers scored by an LLM judge.

openllmleaderboard.text: A Hugging Face leaderboard that re-runs a fixed evaluation setup on every submitted open model. Its first version scored ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, Winogrande and GSM8K through the EleutherAI harness.

osworld.text: 369 computer-use tasks in a real executable desktop environment spanning web and desktop apps, file I/O and multi-application workflows, where an agent controls keyboard and mouse and is scored by execution-based checks.

osworld20.text: 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows in real desktop environments, grounded in authentic input files and stateful user profile data, scored both for full completion and for partial progress.

osworldg.text: A GUI grounding benchmark of 564 finely annotated samples spanning text matching, element recognition, layout understanding and precise manipulation, mapping natural language instructions to actions on a screen.

osworldverified.text: A refined release of OSWorld, the open-ended computer-use benchmark on real desktop and web applications: more than 300 issues in task instructions, timing and grading functions were fixed, and runs moved from local virtual machines to parallel AWS environments.

paperbench.text: 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight and Oral papers that an agent must replicate from scratch, building the codebase and running the experiments, graded against author-co-developed rubrics of 8,316 individually checkable sub-tasks.

perceptiontest.text: About 11.6k purpose-filmed real-world videos with multiple-choice and grounded video questions, object and point tracks and action and sound segments, probing memory, abstraction, physics and semantics across video, audio and text.

piqa.text: A physical commonsense benchmark posing everyday goals with two candidate solutions, where the model must pick the one that actually works given how objects and materials behave.

pixmocount.text: A counting evaluation from the PixMo data family: web images labeled by running the Detic detector and then filtered, where a model reports how many instances of a named object appear. The validation and test splits are human-verified and hold counts from 2 to 10.
